question: True or false: at least two Londoners have exactly the same number of hairs on their heads.
answer: True, by the pigeonhole principle. A scalp carries roughly 100,000 to 150,000 hairs, and nobody has a million, while London has nearly 9 million people. Put 9 million people into fewer than a million possible counts and many counts must be shared, without anyone counting a single hair.
move: More items than boxes guarantees a shared box, with no counting at all.
ask: Which certainty could I reach just by comparing two counts?
trap: Thinking it needs a count of every head to know.
source: Office for National Statistics, mid-2023 population estimates, London
reference: Office for National Statistics, Population estimates for England and Wales: mid-2023, London region
